correctness.rationale: Fresh reconstruction confirms the fixed-numerator orbit formula and both asymptotics, conditional only on the published two-bridge L-space classification premise. For even p, the criterion p≡±1 mod |q| makes the admissible positive canonical q exactly 1 plus nontrivial proper divisors of p−1 and p+1. Because those odd numbers have no nontrivial divisor exceeding (p+1)/3, every such q is in the canonical half-range. Schubert inversion up to mirror sends a divisor to its complementary divisor; the only fixed points are square roots, producing the stated half-orbit correction. The odd-divisor summatory function contributes (1/4)X log X before the final orbit bookkeeping, while the even-totient sum is \(X^2/\pi^2+O(X\log X)\), so \(B(X)\sim X^2/(4\pi^2)\) and \(L(X)/B(X)\sim \pi^2\log X/X\). The package checker is consistent with this proof but was not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The determinant is a canonical complexity parameter for two-bridge links, and the result converts a qualitative classification into an exact per-determinant census plus a global rarity law. The \(X\log X\) versus \(X^2\) separation is a mathematically natural structural consequence of the p−1/p+1 factorization and is more informative than a finite table or a restatement of the classification.

limitations: Counts unoriented two-bridge link types up to mirror and by Schubert numerator/determinant only.
Does not count L-space surgery slopes or address crossing-number/volume density.
